Adds a user authorized for this protected directory. The password is sensitive and is sent in the form POST body.

evidence.note: Pinned /DirectoryPrivacy/add_user declares x-readonly=false. It changes the selected account directory settings or access users, so use form POST. Password inputs, when present, must stay out of query strings.

Pinned /DirectoryPrivacy/configure_directory_protection parameters/0 marks authname required but its description explicitly says "Only use this parameter when you enable password protection." Override only authname requiredness so disabling can omit it. dir and enabled retain pinned requiredness; no runtime cross-field rule is invented. x-readonly=false requires form POST.

notes.text: Available in cPanel 88 and later; operates on the selected account. No request defaults are declared in the pinned operation. Directory paths are sent unchanged and are not normalized by the client.

dir may be an absolute or relative directory path. enabled=true enables password protection; false disables it and is sent as 0. Supply authname only when enabling protection, as documented. authname is optional in this interface because it is conditional in the source prose; the client does not enforce that cross-parameter condition. Empty authname is sent rather than omitted. The source declares clean rollback; the client performs no automatic rollback.

auth_name, auth_type, passwd_file and protected remain optional. protected is an integer 0/1 payload flag distinct from the ordinary UAPI success status: 0 means not protected. Basic and None are documented authentication types. Empty strings remain empty; no nullable fields are inferred.
